title: Genuine Multipartite Entanglement between Logical Qubits via Cross-Code Lattice Surgery
authors: Alex Steiner, Tomasz Andrzejewski, Phila Rembold, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, Christian D. Marciniak, Robert Freund, Ivan Pogorelov, Thomas Monz, Philipp Schindler, Marcel Meyer, Nicolai Friis
abstract: Universal quantum computers are expected to generate arbitrary complex quantum states of logical qubits encoded in many physical qubits. This capability hinges on a fault-tolerantly implemented universal gate set, which no single quantum error-correction code admits transversally but which becomes accessible by joining complementary codes via lattice surgery. Here we report on the experimental generation and certification of logical genuine multipartite entanglement in a trapped-ion quantum processor using a transversally implemented universal logical gate set. The gate set is accessed via lattice surgery across two different codes and comprises a Hadamard gate on a four-qubit surface code and a doubly controlled Pauli-$Z$ ($\overline{\mathrm{CCZ}}$) gate on an eight-qubit 3D colour code. To showcase this lattice-surgery toolbox, we generate both stabiliser (Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger) and non-stabiliser ($|\overline{\mathrm{CCZ}}\rangle$) states of three logical qubits and verify their genuine multipartite entanglement--a form of correlation beyond statistical mixtures of bipartite entanglement across any bipartition. We further use these cross-code primitives to demonstrate arbitrary rotations of single logical qubits via a $\overline{\mathrm{CCZ}}$-based resource gadget accessing the full universal gate set through lattice surgery. Together, these demonstrations showcase the core building blocks of an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computation and its ability to generate complex logical quantum states.
summary: The research demonstrates how to build complex logical quantum operations on trapped ions by merging two different Quantum Error Correction codes via lattice surgery. They successfully generated and verified genuine multipartite entanglement in both stabiliser and non-stabiliser states. This work establishes a core, fault-tolerant building block for future large-scale quantum computers.
main_problem: The goal is to experimentally demonstrate the generation and certification of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) between logical qubits using a fault-tolerant universal gate set.
main_result: The authors successfully generated and certified both stabiliser (GHZ) and non-stabiliser states exhibiting GME, while also demonstrating arbitrary single logical qubit rotations. These results confirm the viability of cross-code lattice surgery for building complex quantum computation primitives.
method: They utilized lattice surgery to combine complementary Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes—specifically a surface code and a 3D colour code—to access a universal gate set transversally.
model_or_system: The experiments were performed on a trapped-ion quantum processor using ${}^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ions. Information is encoded into logical qubits protected by multiple QEC codes, which are merged via lattice surgery operations.
key_observables: Logical state fidelity for GHZ and non-stabiliser states; the stabiliser norm ($D$) to certify GME and non-stabiliserness.
important_parameters: Experimental fidelities (e.g., $F_{	ext{exp.GHZ}} = 83.0\%$), noise parameters ($p_1=0.005, p_2=0.015$), and theoretical thresholds for GME/non-stabiliserness.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the lattice surgery procedure correctly merges the codes to provide fault-tolerant access to gates beyond what any single code supports transversally.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the definition of logical GME, the physical circuits for cross-code lattice surgery (smooth merge M), and the preparation protocols for both GHZ and non-stabiliser states ($	ext{|CCZ}angle$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically details the theoretical necessity of lattice surgery to achieve universal gates, presents the experimental realization on trapped ions using specific codes (SC and CC), demonstrates GME generation for different state types, and concludes with showing arbitrary single-qubit rotations.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, hardware-validated blueprint for scaling quantum computation by solving the fundamental problem of accessing universal gates fault-tolerantly through code combination.
